class.name: DustVolume3D
class.brief_description: A box of still, dusty air: slow-drifting motes that fill a volume.
class.description: A [DustVolume3D] fills its [member size] with dust motes — tiny soft points that drift slowly, fade in and out over their lives, and hang in the air with no gravity. It is a [GPUParticles3D] configured end to end (box emission, mote texture, process material, lifetime), so placing dusty air is one node and a few sliders instead of a particle setup session. The mote count follows from the box: [member density] motes per cubic metre, capped at 4096. The box starts full — the node pre-rolls its particles — so a room is dusty from the first frame. Place a [DustVolume3D] inside a [LightVolume3D] shaft and the motes read as dust caught in the beam; place one across a whole room for air that feels unventilated. Because it is a [GPUParticles3D], everything particles can do (pause, restart, amount ratio) still works; the properties below simply rebuild the setup when changed.

members.member: Motes per cubic metre of the box. The total count is the box's volume times this, capped at 4096.
How fast the motes wander, in metres per second. Dust hangs almost still; values around [code]0.03[/code]–[code]0.1[/code] look like air.
The motes' colour. Warm whites read as dust in sunlight; cool greys as ash or spores.
The diameter of one mote, in metres.
The motes' opacity at the brightest point of their fade-in/fade-out cycle.
The size of the dusty box, in metres.
